h: Five Lights, Six Gifts, and the Oral Torah
The lights of creation and the six restored gifts illuminate the Written Torah and the Six Orders of Mishnah.
Five Mentions of Light and the Five Books of Torah

p: בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה ג, ה): חָמֵשׁ פְּעָמִים "אוֹר" שֶׁנֶּזְכַּר בְּמַאֲמַר "יְהִי אוֹר" כְּנֶגֶד חֲמִשָּׁה חֻמְּשֵׁי תוֹרָה:
— In the Midrash (Bereishit Rabbah 3:5): The five times the word 'light' is mentioned in the creation passage of 'Let there be light' correspond to the Five Books of the Torah:
"וַיֹּאמֶר אֱלֹהִים יְהִי אוֹר" – כְּנֶגֶד סֵפֶר בְּרֵאשִׁית שֶׁבּוֹ נִתְעַסֵּק הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא וּבָרָא עוֹלָמוֹ.
— "'And God said, Let there be light'—corresponds to the Book of Genesis, wherein the Holy One, blessed be He, engaged and created His world."
הַיְינוּ שֶׁנִּצְרְכוּ נְפָשׁוֹת שֶׁיִּהְיוּ כֵּלִים לְקַבָּלַת הָאוֹר,
— That is to say: holy souls were required to serve as receptive vessels for receiving the divine light,
וְהֵם כָּל הַנְּפָשׁוֹת שֶׁעָבְרוּ בְּסֵפֶר בְּרֵאשִׁית בְּהִשְׁתַּלְשְׁלוּת הַדּוֹרוֹת,
— and these are all the souls that unfolded throughout the Book of Genesis across the succession of generations,
עַד שֶׁנּוֹלְדוּ שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר שִׁבְטֵי יָהּ,
— until the twelve tribes of God were born,
וְהֵמָּה הֵם עִיקַּר הַכֵּלִים לְקַבָּלַת הָאוֹר.
— and they are the primary vessels for absorbing the supernal light.
"וַיְהִי אוֹר" – כְּנֶגֶד סֵפֶר וְאֵלֶּה שְׁמוֹת שֶׁבּוֹ יָצְאוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל מֵאֲפֵלָה לְאוֹרָה,
— "'And there was light'—corresponds to the Book of Exodus, wherein Israel emerged from darkness into light,"
וְהַיְינוּ הִתְגַּלּוּת אוֹר הַתּוֹרָה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה;
— which signifies the revelation of the light of the Torah in this world;
וְגָלוּת מִצְרַיִם הַקּוֹדֵם הוּא הֲכָנָה לָזֶה,
— and the preceding Egyptian exile served as the prerequisite preparation for this,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת ה.):
— as they stated (Berakhot 5a):
"שָׁלֹשׁ מַתָּנוֹת וְכוּלֵי עַל יְדֵי יִסּוּרִין, תּוֹרָה וְכוּלֵי".
— 'Three precious gifts, etc., were given through suffering: the Torah, etc.'
"וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים אֶת הָאוֹר כִּי טוֹב" – כְּנֶגֶד סֵפֶר וַיִּקְרָא שֶׁהוּא מָלֵא הֲלָכוֹת רַבּוֹת,
— "'And God saw the light, that it was good'—corresponds to the Book of Leviticus, which is filled with abundant laws,"
וְהַיְינוּ הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת הָאוֹר בְּכָל הַפְּרָטִים.
— which represents the expansion and permeation of the divine light into all minute details.
"וַיַּבְדֵּל אֱלֹהִים בֵּין הָאוֹר וּבֵין הַחֹשֶׁךְ" – כְּנֶגֶד סֵפֶר בַּמִּדְבָּר שֶׁהוּא מַבְדִּיל בֵּין יוֹצְאֵי מִצְרַיִם לְבָאֵי הָאָרֶץ.
— "'And God divided between the light and the darkness'—corresponds to the Book of Numbers, which separates between the generation leaving Egypt and those entering the Promised Land."
הַיְינוּ: דּוֹר הַמִּדְבָּר הֵם נְפָשׁוֹת שֶׁל הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב,
— That is: the generation of the wilderness represents the souls linked to the Written Torah,
דְּשִׁשִּׁים רִבּוֹא אוֹתִיּוֹת בַּתּוֹרָה כַּיָּדוּעַ;
— for there are six hundred thousand letters in the Torah, as is known;
וּבָאֵי הָאָרֶץ הֵם הַנְּפָשׁוֹת דְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
— whereas those entering the Land are the souls connected to the Oral Torah,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ חֵלֶק ב, קלז עַמּוּד ב) דִּמְסָרָהּ לִיהוֹשֻׁעַ – הַיְינוּ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
— as written (holy Zohar Part II, 137b) that Moses transmitted it to Joshua—which signifies the Oral Torah,
דְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב מָסַר לַכֹּהֲנִים בְּנֵי לֵוִי.
— since the Written Torah he entrusted specifically to the Priests, the sons of Levi.
וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא עה.): "פְּנֵי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ כִּפְנֵי לְבָנָה",
— And concerning this they taught (Bava Batra 75a): 'The countenance of Joshua was like the face of the moon,'
וְזֶה נִקְרָא "חֹשֶׁךְ" וְ"לַיְלָה",
— and this reflective aspect is designated 'darkness' and 'night',
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (סַנְהֶדְרִין כד.): "'בְּמַחֲשַׁכִּים הוֹשִׁיבַנִי' – זֶה תַּלְמוּדָהּ שֶׁל בָּבֶל".
— as they expounded (Sanhedrin 24a): "'He has set me in dark places'—this refers to the Babylonian Talmud."
וּבְתַנְחוּמָא (פָּרָשַׁת נֹחַ ג) עַל הַפָּסוּק "'הָעָם הַהֹלְכִים בַּחֹשֶׁךְ רָאוּ אוֹר גָּדוֹל'
— And in Tanchuma (Parashat Noach 3) on the verse: "'The people walking in darkness have seen a great light'—
אוֹר גָּדוֹל שֶׁגְּנָזוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לַעֲמֵלֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה".
— this is the great primordial light that the Holy One hid away for those who toil in the Oral Torah."
וּבְתַרְגּוּם שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים וּבְתַנְחוּמָא (סוֹף פָּרָשַׁת כִּי תִשָּׂא לו),
— And in the Targum of Shir HaShirim and in Tanchuma (end of Ki Tisa 36):
דְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם יָדַע יוֹם וָלַיְלָה,
— that Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, knew the distinction between day and night upon the mount,
שֶׁבַּיּוֹם לָמַד תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב וּבַלַּיְלָה תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה.
— for by day God taught him the Written Torah, and by night the Oral Torah.
"וַיִּקְרָא אֱלֹהִים לָאוֹר יוֹם" – כְּנֶגֶד סֵפֶר מִשְׁנֵה תוֹרָה וְכוּלֵי,
— "'And God called the light Day'—corresponds to the Book of Deuteronomy (Mishneh Torah), etc.,"
שֶׁהוּא כְּעִנְיַן מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְעַל הִשָּׁנוֹת הַחֲלוֹם אֶל פַּרְעֹה פַּעֲמָיִם כִּי נָכוֹן הַדָּבָר וְגוֹמֵר",
— which parallels what is stated (Genesis 41:32): 'And for that the dream was doubled unto Pharaoh twice, it is because the thing is established, etc.,'
וְהַיְינוּ עַל יְדֵי שֶׁנִּשְׁנָה הַדָּבָר פַּעֲמַיִם
— signifying that through the repetition of the matter a second time
נִתְקַיֵּים הָאוֹרָה לְקִיּוּם הָעוֹלָם לִהְיוֹת נִקְרָא "אוֹר יוֹם",
— the illumination was definitively established for the sustenance of the world to be designated the 'light of day',
שֶׁהוּא דָּבָר הַמְבוֹרָר.
— which is a thoroughly clarified, verified matter.

h: Five Emanations and the Divine Flow of Light

p: וְהִנֵּה חֲמִשָּׁה אוֹרוֹת הֵמָּה מִצַּד הַמַּשְׁפִּיעַ
— Now, these five lights stem from the vantage point of the Emanator (haMashpia)
נֶגֶד הַחֲמֵשׁ מִדּוֹת עַד יְסוֹד,
— corresponding to the five divine attributes preceding Yesod (Chesed, Gevurah, Tiferet, Netzach, Hod),
וְהֵמָּה נִשְׁפָּעִים בְּכָל יוֹם מִימֵי הַשָּׁבוּעַ עַל יְדֵי קְדוּשַּׁת שַׁבָּת,
— and they flow forth and are channeled into each day of the week through the holiness of Shabbat,
חוּץ מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת שֶׁהוּא הֲכָנָה עַל שַׁבָּת הַבָּא.
— except for Friday (Erev Shabbat), which serves as the active preparation for the arriving Sabbath.

h: Six Blessings Lost Through Adam’s Sin

p: וְעוֹד אִיתָא בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה יב, ו):
— Furthermore, it is taught in the Midrash (Bereishit Rabbah 12:6):
שִׁשָּׁה דְבָרִים נִטְּלוּ מֵאָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן אַחַר הַקִּלְקוּל:
— Six things were stripped from Adam the First after his degradation:
זִיווֹ, חַיָּיו, וְקוֹמָתוֹ,
— his radiance, his lifespan, and his stature;
פֵּירוֹת הָאָרֶץ – וְהַיְינוּ הַטַּעַם,
— the fruits of the earth—which denotes exquisite taste;
וּפֵירוֹת הָאִילָן – וְהַיְינוּ הָרֵיחַ גַּן עֵדֶן;
— and the fruits of the tree—which is the celestial fragrance of Gan Eden;
וְזֶה שֶׁכָּתַב בְּתַנְחוּמָא (פָּרָשַׁת בְּרֵאשִׁית) תְּמוּרָתוֹ: "וְנִתְגָּרֵשׁ מִגַּן עֵדֶן",
— and this is why Midrash Tanchuma records in its place: 'and he was expelled from Gan Eden',
שֶׁמַּה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה "פֵּירוֹת הָאִילָן" הַכַּוָּנָה גַּם כֵּן פֵּירוֹת גַּן עֵדֶן,
— for what Bereishit Rabbah terms 'fruits of the tree' intends likewise the fruits of Gan Eden,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה מא): "כְּגַן ה' – לָאִילָנוֹת";
— as written (Bereishit Rabbah 41:9): “'Like the garden of Hashem'—with respect to trees';
וְהַמְּאוֹרוֹת.
— and the celestial luminaries.
וְכֻלָּם יַחְזְרוּ לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא.
— And all of them are destined to be fully restored in the World to Come.

— we merit and taste these very six gifts:

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 12:6: “The outgrowths [toledot]” – Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥman said: All toledot that are stated in the Torah are written defectively except for two: “These are the offspring [toledot] of Peretz…” (Ruth 4:18), and this one. Why are those [others] defective? Rabbi Yudan said in the name of Rabbi Avin: They are corresponding to the six things that were taken away from Adam the first man [after he sinned]. They are: His radiance, his [eternal] life, his stature, the [extraordinary] produce of the earth, the [extraordinary] fruit of the tree, and the lights. His radiance, from where is it derived? It is as it is stated: “You alter his countenance and send him away” (Job 14:20). His life, from where is it derived? “For you are dust, [and to dust shall you return]” (Genesis 3:19). His stature, from where is it derived? It is as it is stated: “The man and his wife hid” (Genesis 3:8). Rabbi Abahu said: At that moment, the stature of Adam the first man was reduced and [he] became a [mere] hundred cubits. The produce of the earth and the fruit of the tree, from where is it derived? It is as it is stated: “Cursed is the ground on your account” (Genesis 3:17). As for the lights, Rabbi Shimon ben Rabbi Yehuda of Kefar Akko said in the name of Rabbi Meir: Although the lights were cursed on the day before Shabbat, they were stricken only at the conclusion of Shabbat. This is in accordance with the opinion of the Rabbis and not in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yosei, as Rabbi Yosei said: Adam the first man, his glory did not spend the night with him. What is his source? “Man [adam] will not go to rest in his splendor…” (Psalms 49:13). The Rabbis say: [His glory did spend the night with him; ] only at the conclusion of Shabbat was his radiance taken from him as He expelled him from the Garden of Eden. That is what is written: “He banished the man” (Genesis 3:24), and it is written: “You alter his countenance and send him away” (Job 14:20). Rabbi Yehuda bar Rabbi Simon said: By the light with which the world was created, Adam the first man could look out and see from one end of the world to the other. When the Holy One blessed be He looked ahead at the actions of the generation of Enosh, the actions of the generation of the Flood, and the actions of the generation of the Dispersion, [and saw] that they were corrupt, He arose and hid it away from them, as it is stated: “Their light will be withheld from the wicked” (Job 38:15). Why did He hide it away? The explanation is that he hid it away for the righteous in the future, as it is stated: “God saw that it [light] was good [tov]” (Genesis 1:4). Tov is nothing other than the righteous, as it is stated: “Say of the righteous one that he is good [tov]” (Isaiah 3:10). From where is it derived that He hid it away for the righteous? It is as it is stated: “But the path of the righteous is like a dawning light” (Proverbs 4:18). When he saw that the light was hidden away for the righteous, He rejoiced, as it is stated: “At the light of the righteous He will rejoice” (Proverbs 13:9). Rabbi Levi said in the name of Rabbi Gezeira: That [primordial] light functioned for thirty-six hours – twelve on the day before Shabbat, twelve on the night of Shabbat, and twelve on Shabbat [day]. When Adam the first man sinned, He sought to hide it away [immediately], but He accorded deference to Shabbat, as it is stated: “God blessed the seventh day” (Genesis 2:3). With what did He bless it? It was with light. When the sun set on Shabbat eve the light continued to function. Everyone began praising the Holy One blessed be He. That is what is written: “Under all the heavens they sing His praises” (Job 37:3). Why? It is because “His light is to the ends of the earth” (Job 37:3). That light illuminated all day and all night. As the sun set at the conclusion of Shabbat, darkness began approaching, and at that time Adam the first man became afraid. He said: ‘Is it possible that the one [the serpent] in whose regard it is written: “He will strike your head [yeshufekha], and you will strike his heel [teshufenu]” (Genesis 3:15), is now coming to confront me, as it is stated: “And I said that darkness will envelop me [yeshufeni]”?’ (Psalms 139:11). He said this with bewilderment. What did the Holy One blessed be He do? He prepared for him two flint stones, and he struck them one against the other. Light emerged from them and he recited a blessing over it. That is what is written: “Night, for me, is light” (Psalms 139:11). This is in accordance with the opinion of what was taught in the school of Rabbi Yishmael: Why does one recite at the conclusion of Shabbat the blessing over light: ‘[Blessed be God] Who creates the lights of fire?’ It is because that time was the beginning of its creation. Rav Huna in the name of Rabbi Aivu in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan said: One recites a blessing over it [light] at the conclusion of Yom Kippur, as well, because fire rested on that day. Rabbi Berekhya said in the name of Rabbi Shmuel: Although the [six] items were created in their complete form, when Adam the first man sinned they were ruined, and they will not be restored to their completeness until the descendant of Peretz [the Messiah] comes, as it is stated: “These are the offspring [toledot] of Peretz” (Ruth 4:18) – in its complete form, for the six things [taken away from Adam] that will be restored: His radiance, his [eternal] life, his stature, the produce of the earth, the fruit of the tree, and the lights. His radiance, from where is it derived? It is as it is stated: “May all those who love Him be like the sun coming out in its might” (Judges 5:31). His [eternal] life, from where is it derived? It is as it is stated: “For like the days of a tree will be the days of My people…” (Isaiah 65:22), and it is taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai says: “Tree” is nothing other than Torah, as it says: “It is a tree of life for those who grasp it” (Proverbs 3:18). His stature, from where is it derived? It is as it is stated: “I caused you to walk upright [komemiyut]” (Leviticus 26:13). Rabbi Ḥiyya taught: With upright stature and not in fear of any creature. Rabbi Yudan said: [Their stature will be] one hundred cubits like Adam the first man. Rabbi Shimon said: Two hundred cubits. Rabbi Elazar bar Rabbi Shimon said: Three hundred: Koma refers to one hundred, and meyot – refers to [another] two hundred. Rabbi Abahu said: Nine hundred cubits. Rabbi Berekhya said in the name of Rabbi Dosa: Rabbi Abahu’s source is from here: “For like the days of a tree will be the days of My people” – like a sycamore that grows in the ground for six hundred years. An offspring emerges from its mother’s womb a bit more than a cubit long. Go out and calculate one-and-a-half cubits per year, that is nine hundred cubits. The produce of the earth, the fruit of the tree, from where is it derived? It is as it is stated: “For the seed is of peace: The vine will yield its fruit, [and the land will yield its produce]” (Zechariah 8:12). The lights, from where is it derived? It is as it is written: “The light of the moon will be like the light of the sun [and the light of the sun will be sevenfold, like the light of the seven days]” (Isaiah 30:26).”

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 41:7: ““Lot raised his eyes and saw the entire plain of the Jordan, that it was all watered, before the Lord destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah, like the garden of the Lord, like the land of Egypt, as you come to Tzoar” (Genesis 13:10). “Lot raised his eyes and saw the entire plain of the Jordan” – Rabbi Naḥman bar Ḥanin said: Anyone who has a voracious appetite for sexual immorality will ultimately be fed from his own flesh and blood. Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina said: This entire verse is comprised of expressions of sexual immorality. [“Lot raised his eyes”] – just as it says: “His master's wife raised her eyes [toward Joseph and she said: Lie with me]” (Genesis 39:7). “And saw the entire plain [kikar] of the Jordan, that it was all watered” – just as it says: “For due to a licentious woman, one is brought to a loaf [kikar] of bread” (Proverbs 6:26). “That it was all watered [mashke]” – just as it says: “He shall give the woman to drink [hishka] the bitter water that causes a curse” (Numbers 5:24). “Before the Lord destroyed [shaḥet]” – just as it says: “It was when he consorted with his brother's wife, he would spill [veshiḥet] on to the ground” (Genesis 38:9). “Like the garden of the Lord” – for trees; “like the land of Egypt” – for seeds. “Lot chose for himself all the plain of the Jordan, and Lot journeyed from the east, and each parted from his brother” (Genesis 13:11). “Abram lived in the land of Canaan, and Lot lived in the cities of the plain, and pitched his tent as far as Sodom” (Genesis 13:12). “And the men of Sodom were extremely wicked and sinful to the Lord” (Genesis 13:13). “Lot chose for himself” – Rabbi Yosei ben Zimra said: Like a person selecting his mother’s marriage contract. “Lot journeyed from the east [mikedem]” – he moved himself away from the One who preceded [kadmono] the world. He said: ‘I desire neither Abram nor his God.’ “Each parted from his brother. Abram lived [in the land of Canaan]” – Rabbi Meir says: You do not have among the cities any as evil as Sodom, as when a person is wicked, they refer to him as a person of Sodom. You do not have any among the peoples as tough as the Emorites, as when a person is tough, they refer to him as an Emorite. Rabbi Yosei said: You do not have among the cities any as beautiful as Sodom, as Lot circulated among all the cities of the plain and did not find a place as fine as Sodom, and these [the people of Sodom] were the most distinguished among them – “and the men of Sodom were extremely wicked and sinful to the Lord” (Genesis 13:13). “Wicked” – towards one another; “sinful” – through sexual immorality; “to the Lord” – through idolatry; “extremely” – through bloodshed.”

The Gemara says: There are five matters in our world which are one-sixtieth of their most extreme manifestations. They are: Fire, honey, Shabbat, sleep, and a dream. h: The Radiance and Gifts Restored Through Holiness

p: "זִיווֹ" – הוּא מְאוֹר פָּנִים שֶׁל שַׁבָּת,
— 'His radiance'—this is the glowing countenance of Shabbat,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה יא): "בֵּרְכוֹ בִּמְאוֹר פָּנָיו שֶׁל אָדָם".
— as written (Bereishit Rabbah 11:2): 'He blessed it with the shining countenance of man.'
"חַיָּיו" – כִּדְאִיתָא (יוֹמָא עא.):
— 'His lifespan'—as taught (Yoma 71a):
"'וּשְׁנוֹת חַיִּים וְשָׁלוֹם יוֹסִיפוּ לָךְ' וְכוּלֵי, אֵלּוּ שְׁנוֹתָיו שֶׁל אָדָם הַמִּתְהַפְּכוֹת עָלָיו מֵרָעָה לְטוֹבָה",
— “'And years of life and peace shall they add to you, etc.'—these are a person's years that are transformed from adversity to goodness,'
וְעַל יְדֵי קְדוּשַּׁת שַׁבָּת מִתְהַפְּכוֹת מִיגִיעָה לִמְנוּחָה וְעֹנֶג.
— and through the holiness of Shabbat they are converted from wearying toil into tranquil rest and delight.
"קוֹמָתוֹ" – דְּאִיתָא בַּגְּמָרָא (קִדּוּשִׁין לא.): "אָסוּר לְאָדָם שֶׁיְּהַלֵּךְ בְּקוֹמָה זְקוּפָה",
— 'His stature'—for it is taught in the Gemara (Kiddushin 31a): 'It is forbidden for a man to walk with an erect stature,'
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה שָׁם עַל מִקְרָא זֶה,
— and as written in Bereishit Rabbah there on that verse;
וְהַיְינוּ דִּכְתִיב: "וְהִתְהַלַּכְתִּי בְּתוֹכְכֶם" – אֲטַיֵּיל עִמָּכֶם בְּגַן עֵדֶן,
— meaning as it is written (Leviticus 26:12): 'And I will walk among you'—I will stroll with you in Gan Eden,
מִמֵּילָא יוּכְלוּ לֵילֵךְ בְּקוֹמָה זְקוּפָה
— and consequently souls will then be permitted to walk with upright stature
מֵאַחַר שֶׁאֲטַיֵּיל עִמָּכֶם בְּשָׁוֶה,
— since I shall stroll with you as equals,
כְּאַאֲמָרָם זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ה): "'תַּמָּתִי' – תְּאוֹמָתִי, לֹא זֶה גָּדוֹל מִזֶּה",
— as our Sages of blessed memory stated (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:2): “'My undefiled'—My twin, neither greater than the other';
וּכְעִנְיַן (שָׁם פָּרָשָׁה ג): "לֹא זָז מֵחַבְּבָהּ עַד שֶׁקְּרָאָהּ אֲחוֹתִי".
— and along the lines of (there, parashah 3): 'He did not cease cherishing her until He called her My sister.'
יָכוֹל לֹא תִּירְאוּ מִמֶּנִּי? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: "וְהָיִיתִי לָכֶם לֵאלֹהִים".
— Might you think you shall not revere Me? Therefore Scripture adds: 'and I will be your God.'
וְזֶהוּ גַּם כֵּן עִנְיַן קְדוּשַּׁת שַׁבָּת,
— And this is likewise the spiritual nature of the holiness of Shabbat,
שֶׁהַמִּצְוָה לְעַנְּגוֹ בְּכָל מִינֵי עֹנֶג,
— wherein the commandment is to indulge it with every manner of delight,
וּמִי שֶׁרֹאשׁוֹ כָּפוּף אֵין לוֹ הַרְחָבַת הַדַּעַת לְעַנֵּג אֶת עַצְמוֹ.
— and one whose head is bowed down possesses no expansive peace of mind (harchavat hada'at) to enjoy delight.
"פֵּירוֹת הָאָרֶץ" – הוּא הַטַּעַם הַנִּרְגָּשׁ גַּם כֵּן בִּקְדוּשַּׁת שַׁבָּת,
— 'The fruits of the earth'—this is the heightened flavor experienced likewise in the holiness of Shabbat,
כִּדְאִיתָא (בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה יא)
— as taught in Bereishit Rabbah (parashah 11)
שֶׁעָשָׂה תַּבְשִׁילִין צוֹנְנִין וְעָרַב לוֹ עַל יְדֵי הַטַּעַם שֶׁל שַׁבָּת.
— that the Emperor was served cold dishes and yet found them delicious through the seasoning taste of Shabbat.
"וּפֵירוֹת הָאִילָן" – שֶׁהוּא הָרֵיחַ, הוּא גַּם כֵּן עַל יְדֵי קְדוּשַּׁת שַׁבָּת,
— 'And the fruits of the tree'—which is fragrance, is likewise restored through the holiness of Shabbat,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (שַׁבָּת קיט.): "תַּבְלִין שֶׁל שַׁבָּת רֵיחוֹ נוֹדֵף, עַל יְדֵי תַּבְלִין אֶחָד יֵשׁ לָנוּ וְשַׁבָּת שְׁמוֹ".
— as written in Shabbat (119a): 'The dishes of Shabbat emit sweet fragrance through a certain spice we possess, whose name is Shabbat.'
וּכְתִיב: "כְּרֵיחַ שָׂדֶה אֲשֶׁר בֵּרֲכוֹ ה'"
— And it is written (Genesis 27:27): 'as the smell of a field which Hashem has blessed'—
זֶהוּ שָׂדֶה שֶׁל תַּפּוּחִים כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (תַּעֲנִית כט:),
— this is an orchard of apples, as they taught in Ta'anit (29b),
וּבִבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה סה, כב) אִיתָא עַל פֵּירוּשׁ זֶה: נִכְנְסָה עִמּוֹ גַּן עֵדֶן,
— and in Bereishit Rabbah (65:22) it is stated on this interpretation: the fragrance of Gan Eden entered along with him,
וְהַיְינוּ רֵיחַ גַּן עֵדֶן, חֲקַל תַּפּוּחִין קַדִּישִׁין.
— namely the fragrance of Gan Eden, the holy field of apples.
"וְהַמְּאוֹרוֹת" – הַיְינוּ שֶׁנֶּחְסְרוּ וְנִפְרְדוּ הָאוֹרוֹת מֵאוֹר הַלְּבָנָה,
— 'And the luminaries'—meaning that the lights were diminished and severed from the light of the moon,
שֶׁהוּא מְרַמֵּז עַל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הַמְּקַבֵּל מֵאוֹר הַחַמָּה שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת מַשְׁפִּיעַ, תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב.
— which alludes to the Oral Torah receiving illumination from the sun, the primary source (Mashpia), which is the Written Torah.
וְעַל יְדֵי קְדוּשַּׁת שַׁבָּת נַעֲשׂוּ כְּלוּלִים זֶה בָּזֶה כְּמוֹ לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא,
— And through the holiness of Shabbat they become unified within one another as in the World to Come,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְהָיָה אוֹר הַלְּבָנָה כְּאוֹר הַחַמָּה וְאוֹר הַחַמָּה יִהְיֶה שִׁבְעָתַיִם כְּאוֹר שִׁבְעַת הַיָּמִים",
— as it is stated (Isaiah 30:26): 'Moreover the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun, and the light of the sun shall be sevenfold, as the light of seven days,'
כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה קוֹדֶם הַחֵטְא.
— just as it was prior to the primordial sin.

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 11:2: ““God blessed the seventh day [and sanctified it]” – Rabbi Yishmael said: He blessed it with manna and He sanctified it with manna. He blessed it with manna in that all the days of the week one omer [of manna] would fall, while on the day before Shabbat two omers would fall. He sanctified it with manna, as it did not fall on it [on Shabbat] at all. Rabbi Natan says: He blessed it with manna and sanctified it with a blessing. Rabbi Yitzḥak said: He blessed it with manna and sanctified it through the gatherer. He blessed it with apparel. Rav Huna said: He should change his clothing. Rabbi Ḥiyya said in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan: He should mix [garments]. Avin bar Ḥisdai said: He should lower [his garments]. Rabbi Yirmeya and Rabbi Ze’eira were walking together [on Shabbat], and the outer garment of Rabbi Yirmeya was raised up, but Rabbi Ze’eira lowered his. This shows that one should lower [one’s garments for Shabbat]. Rabbi Elazar says: He blessed it with [the Shabbat] candle, and there was an incident involving me [that illustrates this]. One time I kindled a candle on Shabbat eve, and I came and found it burning at the conclusion of Shabbat, and nothing [of the oil] was diminished. He blessed it with the radiance of a person’s face, He sanctified it with the radiance of a person’s face. The radiance of a person’s face all the days of the week is not comparable to the way it is on Shabbat. He blessed it with the lights. Rabbi Shimon bar Yehuda of Kefar Akko says in the name of Rabbi Shimon: Even though the lights were cursed on the day before Shabbat, they were not stricken until the conclusion of Shabbat. This is in accordance with the opinion of the Rabbis, and not in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Ami, as Rabbi Ami said: Adam the first man, his glory did not spend the night with him. What is the source? “Man [adam] will not go to rest in his splendor; he is like the beasts that perish” (Psalms 49:13). The Rabbis say: His glory did spend the night with him, and only at the conclusion of Shabbat was his radiance taken from him, as He expelled him from the Garden of Eden. That is what is written: “You alter his countenance and send him away” (Job 14:20). When the sun set on Shabbat eve, the Holy One blessed be He sought to put away the [primordial] light, but He accorded honor to Shabbat. That is what is written: “God blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it” – He blessed it with light. When the sun set on Shabbat eve the [primordial] light continued to function. Everyone began praising [God]; that is what is written: “Under all the heavens they sing His praises, and His light is to the ends of the earth” (Job 37:3). Why was this? Because “His light is to the ends of the earth.” Rabbi Yehuda bar Rabbi Simon said: By the light that the Holy One blessed be He created on the first day, a person could look out and see from one end of the world to the other end. When the Holy One blessed be He looked at the people of the generation of the Flood and the people of the generation of the Dispersion, whose actions were to be corrupt, He arose and hid it away and designated it for the righteous in the future. From where is it derived that He hid it away? It is as it is stated: “Their light will be withheld from the wicked, and the upraised arm will be broken” (Job 38:15). And from where is it derived that He designated it for the righteous in the future? It is as it is stated: “But the path of the righteous is like a dawning light, growing brighter until the day is established” (Proverbs 4:18). Rabbi Levi said in the name of Rabbi Ze’eira: That [primordial] light functioned for thirty-six hours – twelve on the day before Shabbat, twelve on the night of Shabbat, and twelve on Shabbat. As the sun set at the conclusion of Shabbat, darkness began approaching, and Adam the first man became afraid, as it is stated: “And I said that darkness will envelop me [yeshufeni]; night for me is light,” (Psalms 139:11) – that one [the serpent] in whose regard it is written: “He will strike your head [yeshufekha], and you will strike his heel [teshufenu]” (Genesis 3:15), is now coming to confront me. What did the Holy One blessed be He do? He prepared for him two flint stones and he struck them one against the other. Light emerged from them and he recited a blessing over it. That is what is written: “Night for me is light.” What blessing did he recite over it? [Blessed be God] Who creates the lights of fire. This is in accordance with the opinion of Shmuel, as Shmuel said: Why does one recite a blessing over light at the conclusion of Shabbat? It is because that time was the beginning of its creation. Rav Huna in the name of Rav and Rabbi Abahu in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan said: One recites a blessing over it [light] at the conclusion of Yom Kippur, as well, because fire rested all that day.”

paragraphs.text: Yoma 71a: ‘The verse states: “For length of days, and years of life, and peace, will they add to you” (Proverbs 3:2). The Gemara asks: Are there years of life and years that are not of life? The Gemara explains: Rabbi Elazar said: “Years of life” refers to good years. As such, these additional years of life referred to in the verse are the years of a person’s life which are transformed for him from bad to good.’

paragraphs.text: Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:2:2: ““It is the sound of my beloved knocking” – by means of Moses when he said: “Moses said: So said the Lord: At about midnight, I will emerge in the midst of Egypt” (Exodus 11:4). “Open for me” – Rabbi Yasa said: The Holy One blessed be He said to Israel: My children, open for Me one opening of repentance like the eye of the needle, and I will open for you openings that wagons and carriages enter through it. Rabbi Tanḥuma, Rabbi Ḥunya, and Rabbi Abbahu [said] in the name of Reish Lakish: It is written: “Desist, and know that I am God…” (Psalms 46:11) – the Holy One blessed be He said to Israel: Desist from your evil actions and know that I am God. Rabbi Levi said: Were Israel to repent even one day, they would be redeemed immediately and the son of David would come immediately. What is the reason? “For He is our God, and we are the people of His flock and the sheep under His hand; today, if you heed His voice” (Psalms 95:7). Rabbi Yudan and Rabbi Levi say: The Holy One blessed be He said to Israel: Desist from your wicked actions and repent in the blink of an eye, “and know that I am God.” “My sister [aḥoti]” – as they were stitched [nitaḥu] to Me in Egypt with the blood of the paschal offering and the blood of circumcision. That is what is written: “I passed you and saw you wallowing in your blood, and I said to you, in your blood you shall live” (Ezekiel 16:6) – this is the blood of the paschal offering. “I said to you, in your blood you shall live” – this is the blood of circumcision (Ezekiel 16:6). “My love [rayati]” – as they fell in love [sheriu] with Me at the sea and said: “This is my God and I will exalt Him” (Exodus 15:2), “the Lord will reign for ever and ever” (Exodus 15:18). “My dove” – at Mara, as from there they were commanded and became distinctive through all the mitzvot, acts of charity, and good deeds, like the dove that is distinctive. That is what is written: “There He instituted for it statutes and ordinances” (Exodus 15:25). “My faultless [tamati]” – My wholehearted ones [tamuti], as they were wholehearted with Me at Sinai, and said: “Everything that the Lord said, we will perform and we will heed” (Exodus 24:7). Rabbi Yannai said: My twin [teomati], as it were; I am not greater than it and it is not greater than I am. Rabbi Yehoshua of Sikhnin [said] in the name of Rabbi Levi: My twin [teomati], just as with twins, if one has a headache his counterpart feels it. So too, as it were, the Holy One blessed be He says: “I am with him in times of trouble” (Psalms 91:15). “For my head is filled with dew” – on the basis of: “The earth quaked, the heavens dripped” (Psalms 68:9). “My locks, drops of night” – on the basis of what is stated: “The clouds dripped water” (Judges 5:4).”

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 65:22: ““He did not recognize him, because his hands were hairy like the hands of his brother Esau, and he blessed him” (Genesis 27:23). “He did not recognize him” – when wicked people were produced from him, he [Isaac] did not recognize them. “His father Isaac said to him: Approach and kiss me, my son” (Genesis 27:26). “Approach and kiss me” – he said to him: ‘You will be adjacent to me in burial, but no other will be adjacent to me in burial.’ “He approached and kissed him, and he smelled the scent of his garments, and blessed him, and said: See, the scent of my son is as the scent of a field that the Lord blessed” (Genesis 27:27). “He approached and kissed him, and he smelled the scent of his garments” – Rabbi Yoḥanan said: There is nothing whose odor is viler than this goat hide, and you say: “He smelled the scent of his garments, and blessed him”? It is, rather, that when our patriarch Jacob entered to his father, the Garden of Eden entered with him. That is what he said to him: “See, the scent of my son is as the scent of a field.” But when Esau entered to his father, Gehenna entered with him, just as it says: “With the arrival of spite, disgrace arrives” (Proverbs 11:2). Another matter, “he smelled the scent of his garments [begadav], and blessed him” – e.g., Yosef Meshita and Yakum of Tzerorot. Yosef Meshita, when the enemies sought to enter the Temple Mount, they said: ‘Let one of them enter, and it will begin with them.’ They said to him: ‘Enter, and whatever you take out is yours.’ He entered and took out a golden candelabrum. They said to him: ‘It is not appropriate for a commoner to make use of this. Instead, enter again, and what you take out is yours.’ He refused. Rabbi Pinḥas said: They offered him taxes for three years, but he refused. He said: ‘Is it not enough that I angered my God once, that I would anger Him a second time?’ What did they do to him? They placed him on a carpenter’s sawhorse and were sawing him. He was shouting and saying: ‘Woe is me that I angered my Creator.’ Yakum of Tzerorot was the son of the sister of Rabbi Yosei ben Yoezer of Tzereida. He was riding a horse on Shabbat. In front of him, a cross on which Jews who observed Shabbat would be crucified was being dragged. He [Yakum of Tzerorot] said to him [Yosei ben Yoezer]: ‘Look at the horse on which my master has me riding, and look at the horse on which your Master has you riding.’ He told him: ‘If so it is for those who anger Him, all the more so for those who perform His will.’ He [also] said to him: ‘If it is so for those who perform his will, all the more so for those who anger him.’ It [his uncle’s words] penetrated him like the venom of a serpent. He went and fulfilled in himself the four court-imposed death penalties – stoning, burning, beheading, and strangulation. What did he do? He brought a beam and stuck it into the ground. He tied a string to it, arranged wood, and surrounded it with a stone fence. He kindled a bonfire before it, stuck a sword in the middle, kindled the fire under the stones, hanged himself from the beam and was strangled. The fire reached him, it severed the string, he fell into the fire, the sword reached him, the fence fell on him, and he was burned. Yosei ben Yoezer of Tzereida dozed and saw his bier floating in the air. He said: ‘That one preceded me by a small amount of time into the Garden of Eden.’”

h: The Six Orders of Mishnah as Receptacles of Light

p: וְהַשִּׁשָּׁה דְבָרִים הַנִּזְכָּרִים הֵם נֶגֶד הֶאָרַת שִׁשָּׁה סִדְרֵי מִשְׁנָה שֶׁבְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁמִּצַּד הַמְקַבֵּל,
— And these six aforementioned restored things correspond to the illumination of the Six Orders of the Mishnah within the Oral Torah from the vantage point of the recipient (haMekabel),
וְלָכֵן בָּאִים בְּמִסְפַּר שִׁשָּׁה
— and for this reason they emerge in the number six,
שֶׁהוּא גַּם כְּנֶגֶד מִדַּת יְסוֹד
— which also corresponds to the attribute of Yesod,
שֶׁהוּא הַמְקַשֵּׁר הַשְׁפָּעַת הַחֲמִשָּׁה אוֹרוֹת לְהַמְקַבֵּל.
— which binds and channels the flow of the five supernal lights unto the recipient.
וְהֵמָּה נִשְׁפָּעִים מִקְּדוּשַּׁת שַׁבָּת לְכָל שֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה.
— And they are infused from the holiness of Shabbat into all six working days of the week.

h: The Six Orders in the Language of the Prophets

p: וְהִנֵּה קְדוּשַּׁת סִדְרֵי מִשְׁנָה אַסְמְכוּהָ חֲכָמֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שַׁבָּת לא.)
— Now, the sanctity of the Orders of the Mishnah our Sages derived (Shabbat 31a)
עַל פָּסוּק "וְהָיָה אֱמוּנַת עִתֶּיךָ חֹסֶן יְשׁוּעֹת חָכְמַת וָדָעַת":
— upon the verse (Isaiah 33:6): 'And the stability of your times shall be a storehouse of salvations, wisdom, and knowledge':

Faith; that is the order of Zera’im, Seeds, in the Mishna, because a person has faith in God and plants his seeds (Jerusalem Talmud). Your times; that is the order of Moed, Festival, which deals with the various occasions and Festivals that occur throughout the year. Strength; that is the order of Nashim, Women. Salvations; that is the order of Nezikin, Damages, as one who is being pursued is rescued from the hands of his pursuer. Wisdom; that is the order of Kodashim, Consecrated Items. And knowledge; that is the order of Teharot, Purity, which is particularly difficult to master. And even if a person studies and masters all of these, “the fear of the Lord is his treasure,” it is preeminent.”

p: "אֱמוּנַת" – זֶה סֵדֶר זְרָעִים,
— "'Stability/Faith' (Emunat)—this refers to the Order of Zera'im (Seeds),
שֶׁמַּאֲמִין בְּחֵי עוֹלָמִים וְזוֹרֵעַ (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתְבוּ תּוֹסָפוֹת).
— for he believes in the Life of the Worlds and sows (as Tosafot wrote).
וְלִכְאוֹרָה גַּם הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת זוֹרְעִין אַף שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם אֱמוּנָה!
— Now seemingly, idolaters also sow even though they lack faith!
רַק זֶהוּ דַּוְוקָא הָרְבוּתָא מֵאֱמוּנַת יִשְׂרָאֵל:
— Rather, precisely this is the magnificent virtue of the faith of Israel:
הֲגַם שֶׁעוֹשֶׂה מַעֲשָׂיו שֶׁעַל פִּי דֶּרֶךְ הַטֶּבַע מְחַיֵּיב כֵּן
— even though he performs physical tasks that the natural order seemingly dictates,
כְּעִנְיַן הַזְּרִיעָה שֶׁהוּא מַצְמִיחַ שֶׁעוֹלָם כְּמִנְהָגוֹ נוֹהֵג,
— such as agricultural sowing where things sprout as nature takes its course,
עִם כָּל זֶה יוֹדֵעַ בֶּטַח שֶׁהַכֹּל הוּא מֵהַשְׁגָּחַת הַבּוֹרֵא,
— nonetheless he knows with complete certitude that everything is directed by the Creator's providence,
אֲפִילּוּ דָּבָר הַנֶּעֱזָב לִפְעֻלַּת הָאָדָם.
— even a matter seemingly left to human initiative.
"עִתֶּיךָ" – זֶה סֵדֶר מוֹעֵד,
— "'Your times' (Itekha)—this refers to the Order of Moed (Festivals),
שֶׁיֵּשׁ עִתִּים וּזְמַנִּים קְבוּעִים לַעֲבוֹדָה,
— in that there are designated times and seasons dedicated to divine service,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שַׁבָּת י.): "זְמַן תּוֹרָה לְחוּד וּזְמַן תְּפִלָּה לְחוּד".
— as they stated (Shabbat 10a): 'The time for Torah is distinct, and the time for prayer is distinct.'
"חֹסֶן" – זֶה סֵדֶר נָשִׁים,
— "'Strength' (Chosen)—this refers to the Order of Nashim (Women),
שֶׁזֶּהוּ עִנְיַן תּוֹקֶף וּגְבוּרָה,
— for this represents inner power and strength,
כְּאַאֲמָרָם זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (אָבוֹת פֶּרֶק ד מִשְׁנָה א): "אֵיזֶהוּ גִבּוֹר? הַכּוֹבֵשׁ אֶת יִצְרוֹ".
— as our Sages of blessed memory stated (Avot 4:1): 'Who is mighty? He who conquers his evil inclination.'
"יְשׁוּעֹת" – זֶה סֵדֶר נְזִיקִין,
— "'Salvations' (Yeshu'ot)—this refers to the Order of Nezikin (Damages),
כִּי עִיקַּר צֹרֶךְ הַיְשׁוּעָה הוּא עַל אַרְבָּעָה אֲבוֹת נְזִיקִין
— for the primary need for divine salvation is against the four primary categories of damages
הַבָּאִים עַל יְדֵי שְׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִיסָּה.
— which arise through the leaven in the dough (the base inclination).

h: The Four Exiles and the Four Injurious Traits

p: וְהֵמָּה נֶגֶד אַרְבַּע גָּלִיּוֹת
— And these four correspond to the four historical empires and exiles
הַשּׁוֹלְטִים עַל נַפְשׁוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל מִבְּחִינַת אַרְבַּע מִדּוֹת הָרָעוֹת שֶׁבַּנֶּפֶשׁ,
— that dominate over the souls of Israel through the four base traits in the psyche,
וְהֵם: עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, קִנְאָה, תַּאֲוָה, וְכָבוֹד
— and they are: idolatry, jealousy, lust, and honor—
שֶׁהוּא כַּעַס, וְתַאֲוָה, וְהִתְנַשְּׂאוּת:
— which manifest as anger, illicit desire, and haughtiness:
בָּבֶל כְּנֶגֶד כֹּחַ עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה,
— Babylonia corresponds to the spiritual archetype of idolatry,
שֶׁעָשָׂה צֶלֶם דִּדְהַב,
— for Nebuchadnezzar erected the image of gold,
וּבָזֶה שָׁלַט וְהֶחֱרִיב אֶת הַבַּיִת הָרִאשׁוֹן,
— and through this force he held dominion and destroyed the First Temple,
שֶׁהָיָה בָּהֶם יִצְרָא דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
— in which era there existed within Israel the impulse for idolatry
עַד שֶׁבִּיטְּלוּהוּ אַנְשֵׁי כְּנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב יוֹמָא סט:).
— until the Men of the Great Assembly eradicated it (as written in Yoma 69b).
מַלְכוּת מָדַי כְּנֶגֶד תַּאֲוָה,
— The Kingdom of Media corresponds to lust,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת ח:): "בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה דְבָרִים אֲנִי אוֹהֵב אֶת הַפַּרְסִיִּים וְכוּלֵי וּצְנוּעִין בְּדָבָר אַחֵר",
— as they stated (Berakhot 8b): 'For three things I love the Persians, etc., and they are modest in marital intimacy,'
וְהֲגַם שֶׁדָּבָר זֶה הוּא כִּפְרִישׁוּת,
— and even though this practice seems like saintly restraint,
בֶּאֱמֶת הוּא בְּהֵיפֶךְ:
— in truth it is quite the reverse:
עַל יְדֵי שֶׁהֵם שְׁטוּפִים כָּל כָּךְ בְּהַתַּאֲוָה, עַל יְדֵי זֶה בּוֹשִׁים עַצְמָם מִזֶּה.
— because they are so utterly inundated in lust, they consequently feel disgraced and ashamed by it.
וְלָכֵן נִסְמַךְ אַחַר כָּךְ בַּגְּמָרָא:
— And therefore it is juxtaposed immediately afterward in the Gemara:
"'אֲנִי צִוֵּיתִי לִמְקֻדָּשָׁי' – אֵלּוּ הַפַּרְסִיִּים הַמְקֻדָּשִׁים וְהַמְזֻמָּנִים לְגֵיהִנָּם",
— “'I have commanded My consecrated ones' (Isaiah 13:3)—these are the Persians who are consecrated and designated for Gehenna,'
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁהֲגַם שֶׁעַל הַגָּוֶון נִרְאֶה כִּקְדוּשָׁה,
— meaning that even though on the surface it displays an appearance of holiness,
וְיִשְׂרָאֵל נִקְרְאוּ קְדוֹשִׁים בִּשְׁבִיל צְנִיעוּת זֶה (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב שַׁבָּת פו.),
— and Israel are titled holy for genuine modesty (as written in Shabbat 86a),
וְהֵם אַדְּרַבָּה, עַל יְדֵי זֶה מְקֻדָּשִׁים לְגֵיהִנָּם.
— yet they, on the contrary, are designated for Gehenna through it.
וְיָוָן הוּא בְּחִינַת גַּאֲוָה וְהִתְנַשְּׂאוּת
— And Greece embodies pride and arrogant haughtiness
עַל יְדֵי שֶׁהֵם חֲכָמִים בְּעֵינֵיהֶם,
— in that they are wise in their own eyes,
וְזֶה עִנְיַן חָכְמַת יְוָנִית – חָכְמָה חִיצוֹנִית.
— and this is the essence of Greek philosophy—external alien wisdom.
וֶאֱדוֹם הוּא בְּחִינַת כַּעַס וּרְצִיחָה.
— And Edom (Rome) is the archetype of wrath and murderous bloodshed.

h: The Four Forms of Damage as Spiritual Symbols

p: וְיֵשׁ לוֹמַר בִּפְרָטֵי אֲבוֹת נְזִיקִין גַּם כֵּן מְרַמְּזִים עַל זֶה:
— And one can suggest that the specific primary categories of damages likewise allude to these:
"שׁוֹר" הוּא בְּחִינַת הִתְנַשְּׂאוּת – נְגִיחָה בַּקֶּרֶן.
— 'Ox' corresponds to haughtiness—goring with the horn.
"בּוֹר" – בְּחִינַת עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, בֹּארוֹת נִשְׁבָּרִים.
— 'Pit'—corresponds to idolatry, 'broken cisterns' (Jeremiah 2:13).
"מַבְעֶה" – אִיכָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר זֶה הַשֵּׁן, וְהוּא עִנְיַן תַּאֲוַת אֲכִילָה.
— 'Maveh' (tooth/spoil)—according to the opinion that it is the tooth, reflects the lust of consumption.
"הַבְעֵר" – אֵשׁ תַּבְעֵרַת הַכַּעַס.
— 'Fire'—the blaze and fury of wrath.

h: Kodashim and Taharot: Wisdom, Knowledge, and Purity

p: "חָכְמַת" – זֶה סֵדֶר קָדָשִׁים,
— "'Wisdom' (Chokhmat)—this refers to the Order of Kodashim (Holy Offerings),
כִּי קֹדֶשׁ הוּא חָכְמָה כַּיָּדוּעַ בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ.
— for Kodesh (Holiness) is Chokhmah, as is known in the holy Zohar.
"וָדָעַת" – זֶה סֵדֶר טְהָרוֹת,
— "'And knowledge' (Vada'at)—this refers to the Order of Tohorot (Purities);
דַּעַת הוּא רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ,
— for Da'at signifies the Holy Spirit (Ruach HaKodesh),
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּפֵירוּשׁ רַשִּׁ"י תִּשָּׂא (שְׁמוֹת ל"א, ג) עַל פָּסוּק "וָאֲמַלֵּא אֹתוֹ וְגוֹמֵר וּבְדָעַת".
— as written in Rashi's commentary on Ki Tisa (Exodus 31:3) on the verse 'and I have filled him, etc., and with knowledge.'
וּלְרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ אִי אֶפְשָׁר לָבוֹא רַק עַל יְדֵי טָהֳרַת הַלֵּב,
— And unto the Holy Spirit it is impossible to arrive except through the purification of the heart,
וְעַל זֶה בִּקֵּשׁ דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם: "לֵב טָהוֹר בְּרָא לִי אֱלֹהִים",
— and concerning this King David, peace be upon him, pleaded: 'Create in me a clean heart, O God' (Psalms 51:12),
מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהָיָה הוּא רַבָּן שֶׁל בַּעֲלֵי רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ,
— because he was the master of all possessors of the Holy Spirit,
וְהוּא הַתְחָלַת הַכְּתוּבִים שֶׁנֶּאֶמְרוּ בְּרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ כַּיָּדוּעַ.
— and he marks the inception of the Writings (Ketuvim) which were uttered through the Holy Spirit, as is known.
